text:
Jonatan Berggren has found a real job in St. Louis since the Blues claimed him off waivers from Detroit last December. Saturday's two goals against New Jersey, one on a breakaway and one into an empty net, took him to 5 goals and 9 points in 20 games, with three of the points on the power play.

The process is better than it was in Detroit. He's generating 0.87 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his chances), up from 0.55 last season, and his finishing is about where it should be: 5 goals on 4.1 expected. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, from a small nine-game sample, had him taking a lot of shots off passes across the slot and leaving the zone with possession on 62% of his exits.

The caution is the role. He's missed three of the Blues' last ten games, and his ice time is down more than a minute over that stretch, to about 13:34. For a winger whose game is chances off good passes, the minutes and linemates matter more than anything. Our projection: 27 to 45 points.
